content.text: save auth token: save token to keyring: The name org.freedesktop.secrets was not provided by any .service files

That error means your Linux session has no Freedesktop Secret Service provider running, so the keyring API has nowhere to store the token.

Install/start one of these:

```bash
# Debian/Ubuntu
sudo apt install gnome-keyring libsecret-tools
```

Then start it in your session:

```bash
eval "$(gnome-keyring-daemon --start --components=secrets)"
export SSH_AUTH_SOCK
```

Verify:

```bash
secret-tool store --label="test" test key
secret-tool lookup test key
```

If you are on Nix/devenv, add something like:

```nix
packages = [
  pkgs.gnome-keyring
  pkgs.libsecret
];
```

Then restart your shell/session and retry saving the auth token.

If this is a headless SSH session, the clean fix is to run a real secret-service daemon in the user session. The workaround is to configure the tool to use a file/plaintext credential store if it supports one, but that is less secure.
